long_biography.plain_text:
Buying control of a small Florida video chain gave Wayne Huizenga a second arena for the acquisition method he had developed in waste hauling. He expanded Blockbuster by purchasing local operators, standardising stores and recasting the business as a family-oriented national brand. The chain grew from a handful of outlets into the world's largest home-video rental company before its sale to Viacom.

That model rested on experience gained before dawn in Pompano Beach. Huizenga drove rubbish routes, spent afternoons seeking customers and built his own hauling business from a used truck. He later combined it with relatives' Chicago operation to form Waste Management, then served as president and chief operating officer as the company consolidated smaller haulers. The same appetite for scale subsequently shaped his work in car retail, waste services and extended-stay lodging.
